You are agent_4, one of 4 agents (agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, agent_4) working together on one math problem.

## How you work
You call tools; they run in the order you call them, and you see their results in your next response. There is no turn limit. You stop by ending a response without calling a tool. If a teammate tags you, or replies in a thread you're in, after you stop, you are woken and carry on.

## Execution environment
You have your own Python scratchpad file, scratchpad.py: you can read, write, edit and run it. Each run is a fresh Python process, and may take up to 6 hours; while it runs you see nothing on Slack, and what it holds in memory is lost when it ends. A run may use 5 GB of memory in all and write files of up to 8 GB each, and it may use multiprocessing with up to 2 worker processes (no more: it is killed if it has more processes at once).
Next to it is workspace/, a folder the whole team shares: every agent's runs can read and write it, and what one writes there the others can use at once. Put code and results that others can reuse there (for example shared code in workspace/tools.py, or results in workspace/results.json), import shared code with `sys.path.insert(0, "workspace")`, and say on Slack what you put there. Don't overwrite a file someone else wrote: write your own.
The Python environment includes NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, NetworkX, pandas, scikit-learn, gmpy2, Z3, mpmath and SageMath. Sage is imported in the same interpreter (`from sage.all import *`), and GAP and PARI work through it; Sage's Singular-based multivariate ideal methods (such as groebner_basis) crash here, so use SymPy's groebner for those.
There is no public internet access or web search. Do not try to access websites, remote APIs, or install packages. A run cannot start other programs, except more Python processes for multiprocessing.

## Slack
The team shares one Slack channel, #proof. slack_post posts to it, or replies in a message's thread; write @name to tag a teammate. slack_read shows what you haven't read, and after each response you are told when something is waiting. The lead, a person, may post too.
Use the channel to work as a team: split the work, and claim a piece before you start on it so that nobody duplicates it; keep the discussion of one piece in its thread; post each result as soon as it is checked (what was shown, and where in workspace/ its code is); and tag the teammate you need something from.

For an integer \(t\ge 2\), consider all integers \(k\ge t\), finite sets \(V\), and families \(\mathcal F\) of \(k\)-element subsets of \(V\) with the following properties. The family is intersecting, meaning that \(F\cap F'\ne\varnothing\) for all \(F,F'\in\mathcal F\). Its covering number is \(t\), where the covering number is the minimum cardinality of a set \(C\subseteq V\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal F\).

In addition, choose a partition \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal F_t\) into nonempty subfamilies and pairwise disjoint nonempty sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\subseteq V\) such that \(X_i\subseteq F\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F_i\). Define
\[
b(t)=\min\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|X_i|\bigr),
\]
where the minimum ranges over all the choices just described, including \(k\) and \(V\).

With \(\log\) denoting the natural logarithm, determine the exact value of
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\t\in\mathbb Z}}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}.
\]

The answer was proved recently, so it is not an open problem: your team's task is to find it and prove it, completely, and to write Python that really computes or checks every step that can be checked. Printing what you believe is not evidence. Arriving at an answer that settles less than the question asks (a partial or conditional answer, "not known") is not acceptable, and neither is conceding: when an approach fails, try another.

Proving it means showing that the answer is right in every case the question covers, and that no other answer is. Split the work, and the pieces of each part, between you on Slack.

Stop only when the team's proof is complete. Before you stop, post on Slack what you proved, and what is left.

Your conversation was compacted after it reached about 242k tokens (compaction 1): what came before your last few responses has been replaced by the handoff you wrote, below. Slack's history is all still there (slack_read with thread=<id> shows a whole thread, include_read=true the latest messages), and so are your files and workspace/.

## SELF-HANDOFF (agent_4)

We are a team of 4 solving user’s exact asymptotic exponent problem for
\[
b(t)=\min \sum_{i=1}^t (k-|X_i|)
\]
over intersecting uniform families with covering number exactly \(t\), partitioned into \(t\) nonempty classes with pairwise disjoint nonempty common cores \(X_i\).

**We have NOT solved the main problem.** Strongest rigorous current bounds:
\[
c\,t^{3/2}\le b(t)\le (3+o(1))t^{5/3}.
\]
We do not know whether exact exponent is \(5/3\), golden ratio \(\phi\), or something else. Do not assert one without proof. User explicitly insists full answer and no conceding. Team has been working for a long time; no human hint replied.

### Current work / most recent result / next plan

Lead agent_1 asked me (#285) to compute the “bad coalitions” after deleting an actual point in the newly discovered \(5/3\) upper construction. I completed this exactly and posted #289, then derived general degree argument #292. Agent_2 independently duplicated and agrees (#291).

**Most recent result (#292):** In the clean graph-star \(5/3\) construction, initially deleting any actual point has bad-coalition hitting number \(\lambda_v\le 1\), NOT \(\sim h\). If point is an owner graph edge, \(\lambda_v=0\). If it is a non-owner edge, any bad coalition contains all owner edges in the connected component of an endpoint, so one owner color hits all bad coalitions. This extends all regular owner graphs \(G\), not just small \(h\). Larger pruning cost may arise only after multiple point deletions/class discards. Agent_2 is also drafting same general proof. Likely useful next step is study iterated pruning of the star construction to see when \(\lambda\) becomes large, or use this structure for lower bound / possible golden-ratio recursion.

## Core facts proved by team

### 1. Hall-type exact covering property

Write \(P_F=F\setminus X_i\) for \(F\in\mathcal F_i\), \(d_i=k-|X_i|\).

For every subset \(I\subseteq[t]\),
- \(\tau(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)=|I|\): upper by one core representative per class; lower otherwise add reps outside \(I\).
- \(\tau(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal P_i)\ge |I|\), where \(\mathcal P_i=\{P_F:F\in\mathcal F_i\}\): cover petals with fewer than \(|I|\), then cover other classes by core reps.
- Equivalent cover activation: for any point set \(C\), number of classes whose **whole** family is covered by \(C\) is \(\le |C|\).

Can enlarge each \(X_i\) to full intersection of its class; maximal cores remain disjoint, since common point of two classes yields cover \(t-1\).

Can add arbitrarily many private new core points to each class, increasing \(k\) and \(|X_i|\) equally; deficits unchanged, \(\tau\) unchanged. This means huge/private core padding is free.

Deleting a chosen point \(p\in X_i\): delete class \(i\), restrict other classes to members avoiding \(p\). All \(t-1\) remaining classes nonempty and covering number exactly \(t-1\). Cores stay, deficits unchanged. Slack #170 etc.

### 2. Elementary lower exponent \(3/2\)

Let total deficit \(D=\sum d_i\). At least \(m\ge t/2\) classes have \(d_i\le d=2D/t\).
Take maximal rainbow matching of pairwise disjoint petals from those low-deficit classes, size \(r\).

- Selected full sets intersect, disjoint petals imply each class pair has one petal hitting opposite core. Each petal hits at most \(d\) disjoint cores, hence
  \(\binom r2\le rd\), so \(r\le 2d+1\).
- Union \(U\) of matched petals covers every unmatched low-deficit class’s petal family by maximality; \(|U|\le rd\). Add core reps for matched and outside classes; \(\tau=t\) gives \(m\le r(d+1)\).
- Thus \(t/2\le(2d+1)(d+1)\), yielding \(D=\Omega(t^{3/2})\).

Agent_3 has a fully written proof and actual checks:

- `workspace/agent3_lower_check.json`
A simple explicit constant \(b(t)\ge t^{3/2}/20\) for \(t\ge4\) checked numerically and analytically.

### 3. Tournament upper, exact small values

Any tournament on \(t\) classes: choose disjoint large cores; class \(i\) includes its core plus arbitrary one point from each outneighbor core. Intersecting, \(\tau=t\), deficits outdegrees, total \(\binom t2\). Simple uniformization initially choose \(k=2t\), \(|X_i|=2t-d_i\ge t+1\); all target choices avoid any cover \(<t\).

Agent_3 improved to **\(k=t\)** exactly, cores \(|X_i|=\operatorname{indeg}(i)+1=t-\operatorname{outdeg}(i)\). Cover proof:
- For a cover \(C\), let \(A\) be cores met, \(B\) cores exhausted.
- Every \(i\notin A\) must have an outneighbor in \(B\), else a member of class \(i\) avoids \(C\).
- \(t-|A|\le\sum_{j\in B}\operatorname{indeg}(j)\).
- \(|C|\ge |A|+\sum_{j\in B}(|X_j|-1)\ge t\).

### 4. Main breakthrough: rigorous \(5/3\) upper construction

Discovered by me (#234) and crucial optimization corrected by agent_2 (#236). Full proof agent_2 #238/#245/#247/#248.

Choose integer \(h\ge2\).
Let \(G\) be disjoint union of \(h\) copies of \(K_{h,h}\).
- number centers \(n=2h^2\)
- degree \(h\)
- owner classes are graph edges \(e=ab\in E(G)\)
- number classes \(T=nh/2=h^3\).

Actual ground points are **all edges of complete graph \(K_n\)**.
For owner \(ab\), actual petal family contains:
- every \(r\)-subset of \(\operatorname{star}(a)\setminus\{ab\}\),
- every \(r\)-subset of \(\operatorname{star}(b)\setminus\{ab\}\),
where
\[
r=n-h-1=2h^2-h-1.
\]
Each actual petal has a unique center (r large). In full star of n−1 edges, it omits exactly \(h\) edges/neighbor-centers, including owner partner.

**Hall property for actual petals:** For any actual point set \(C\subseteq E(K_n)\), it hits **all** petals of owner \(ab\) iff
\[
\deg_C(a)-1_{\{ab\in C\}}\ge h,\qquad
\deg_C(b)-1_{\{ab\in C\}}\ge h.
\]
If a class is covered, both endpoints lie in \(S=\{a:\deg_C(a)\ge h\}\). Hence number covered classes
\[
\le |E(G[S])|\le h|S|/2\le \sum_{a\in S}\deg_C(a)/2\le |C|.
\]
Thus augmented petals \(\{c_{ab}\}\cup P\) with private color label \(c_{ab}\) have covering number \(T\), and Hall for every color subset.

**Target labels:** For petal \(P\) centered at a, let omitted neighbor set \(O(P)\) (size h). Target every owner edge of \(G\) incident to some vertex in \(O(P)\), except own owner \(ab\). At most \(h^2-1\) target colors. Fill arbitrarily to exactly \(h^2-1\) distinct other colors; possible since \(T-1\ge h^2-1\).

- Two petals with same center intersect because \(2r>n-1\).
- Two with different centers a,c intersect iff actual point ac belongs to both. If disjoint, at least one omits the other center, so targets the other’s owner class.

Now create **new disjoint huge cores** \(X_e\) (size \(T\) suffices in agent_2 clean version; can take larger if desired). Each full member of owner e:
- contains whole \(X_e\),
- contains actual petal P,
- contains arbitrary one point from every target core.
All target choices included. Uniform deficit
\[
D_h=r+(h^2-1)=3h^2-h-2.
\]
Uniform rank \(k=T+D_h\).

Intersections: actual intersection or target visiting opposite whole core. Classes are distinct since each has full own core and at most one point in others.

Cover number \(T\): for any <T point cover, no huge core exhausted, and target choices can avoid selected core points. If selected actual points cover some classes wholly, number of those ≤ number actual selected points; remaining classes require own core reps, so total ≥T. No private padding needed because fill target sets to equal size.

Thus
\[
b(h^3)\le h^3(3h^2-h-2).
\]
For arbitrary t, choose \(h=\lceil t^{1/3}\rceil\), restrict to any t classes of T-class configuration. Exact subunion-cover property gives \(\tau=t\). Hence
\[
b(t)\le(3+o(1))t^{5/3}.
\]

1	import itertools,z3,time,json
     2	start=time.time();h=2;n=2*h*h
     3	G=[]
     4	for block in range(h):
     5	 L=list(range(2*h*block,2*h*block+h));R=list(range(2*h*block+h,2*h*(block+1)))
     6	 G += [(a,b) for a in L for b in R]
     7	actual=list(itertools.combinations(range(n),2));eid={e:j for j,e in enumerate(actual)};t=len(G)
     8	families=[]
     9	for a,b in G:
    10	 fam=[]
    11	 for c,other in [(a,b),(b,a)]:
    12	  star=[eid[tuple(sorted((c,x)))] for x in range(n) if x not in (c,other)]
    13	  fam += [tuple(P) for P in itertools.combinations(star,n-h-1)]
    14	 families.append(fam)
    15	res=[]
    16	for vpair in [(0,2),(0,1),(0,4)]:
    17	 v=eid[vpair];pruned=[[P for P in fam if v not in P] for fam in families]
    18	 vs=[z3.Bool('x%d'%i) for i in range(len(actual)+t)];bad=[]
    19	 for mask in range(1,1<<t):
    20	  I=[i for i in range(t) if mask>>i&1]
    21	  s=z3.Solver()
    22	  s.add(z3.PbLe([(x,1) for x in vs],len(I)-1))
    23	  for i in I:
    24	   for P in pruned[i]:s.add(z3.Or(vs[len(actual)+i],*[vs[p] for p in P]))
    25	  if s.check()==z3.sat:bad.append(mask)
    26	 minimal=[b for b in bad if not any(c!=b and c&b==c for c in bad)]
    27	 assert all(a&b for a in minimal for b in minimal)
    28	 hits=[]
    29	 for k in range(t+1):
    30	  hits=[T for T in itertools.combinations(range(t),k) if all(any(b>>i&1 for i in T) for b in minimal)]
    31	  if hits:break
    32	 item=dict(point=vpair,bad_count=len(bad),minimal_bad=[[i for i in range(t) if b>>i&1] for b in minimal],lambda_v=k,min_hitting_sets=hits)
    33	 res.append(item);print(item,flush=True)
    34	with open('workspace/agent4_star_badcoalitions_h2.json','w') as f:json.dump({'owners':G,'results':res},f,indent=2)
    35	with open('workspace/agent4_star_badcoalitions_h2.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())
    36	print('elapsed',time.time()-start)

import itertools,z3,time,random,json
start=time.time();rng=random.Random(34567)
h=3;n=2*h*h
G=[]
for block in range(h):
 L=range(2*h*block,2*h*block+h);R=range(2*h*block+h,2*h*(block+1));G += [(a,b) for a in L for b in R]
actual=list(itertools.combinations(range(n),2));eid={e:j for j,e in enumerate(actual)};inc=[[i for i,e in enumerate(actual) if a in e] for a in range(n)]
def compute(deleted,colors):
 cs=[z3.Bool('c%d'%p) for p in range(len(actual))];ys={i:z3.Bool('y%d'%i) for i in colors}
 solver=z3.Solver()
 for p in deleted:solver.add(z3.Not(cs[p]))
 for i in colors:
  a,b=G[i];ab=eid[a,b]
  for x in (a,b):
   threshold=h-len(set(inc[x])&deleted)+(ab in deleted)
   solver.add(z3.Implies(ys[i],z3.PbGe([(cs[p],1) for p in inc[x] if p!=ab],threshold)))
 solver.add(z3.PbGe([(y,1) for y in ys.values()]+[(c,-1) for c in cs],1))
 def findbad(allowed):
  if solver.check(*[z3.Not(ys[i]) for i in colors if i not in allowed])==z3.unsat:return None
  model=solver.model();I=[i for i in colors if z3.is_true(model.eval(ys[i]))]
  return I
 cuts=[];opt=z3.Optimize();ds={i:z3.Bool('d%d'%i) for i in colors};opt.minimize(z3.Sum([z3.If(x,1,0) for x in ds.values()]))
 while True:
  assert opt.check()==z3.sat;model=opt.model();drop=[i for i in colors if z3.is_true(model.eval(ds[i]))]
  bad=findbad(set(colors)-set(drop))
  if bad is None:return drop,cuts
  for i in list(bad):
   sub=findbad(set(bad)-{i})
   if sub is not None:bad=sub
  cuts.append(bad);opt.add(z3.Or([ds[i] for i in bad]))
results=[]
for trial in range(12):
 colors=list(range(len(G)));deleted=set();order=list(range(len(actual)));rng.shuffle(order)
 for p in order:
  if not colors:break
  deleted.add(p);drop,cuts=compute(deleted,colors)
  item=dict(trial=trial,point=actual[p],deleted=[actual[v] for v in sorted(deleted)],colors=colors[:],drop=drop,lambda_v=len(drop),cuts=cuts)
  results.append(item)
  if len(drop)>1:print('trial',trial,'depth',len(deleted),'colors',len(colors),'lambda',len(drop),flush=True)
  colors=[i for i in colors if i not in drop]
print('maxlambda',max(x['lambda_v'] for x in results),'runtime',time.time()-start,flush=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_random_pruning_star_h3.json','w') as f:json.dump(dict(h=h,G=G,results=results),f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent4_random_pruning_star_h3.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())

for c in sizes:cores.append(set(range(base,base+c)));base+=c
n=base;t=4;d=[t-c for c in sizes]
families=[]

vs=[[z3.Bool('e%d_%d'%(i,j)) for j in range(len(fam))] for i,fam in enumerate(families)]
s=z3.Solver();s.set(timeout=120000)
for v in vs:s.add(z3.Or(v))
# valid first-edge symmetry
s.add(vs[0][next(j for j,E in enumerate(families[0]) if E==cores[0]|{3})])
good={};conf=0
for i in range(t):
 for j in range(i):
  for a,E in enumerate(families[i]):
   for b,F in enumerate(families[j]):
    meet=E&F
    good[i,a,j,b]=bool(meet) and (meet<=cores[i] or meet<=cores[j])
    if not meet:s.add(z3.Or(z3.Not(vs[i][a]),z3.Not(vs[j][b])));conf+=1
for C in itertools.combinations(range(n),t-1):s.add(z3.Or([vs[i][a] for i in range(t) for a,E in enumerate(families[i]) if not set(C)&E]))
forbidden=0
for choices in itertools.product(*[range(len(fam)) for fam in families]):
 if any(not families[i][choices[i]]&families[j][choices[j]] for i in range(t) for j in range(i)):continue
 score=sum(good[i,choices[i],j,choices[j]] for i in range(t) for j in range(i))
 if score>=5:s.add(z3.Or([z3.Not(vs[i][a]) for i,a in enumerate(choices)]));forbidden+=1
print('built',list(map(len,families)),'conf',conf,'forbidden',forbidden,'time',time.time()-start,flush=True)
status=s.check();out=dict(status=str(status),sizes=sizes,counts=list(map(len,families)),conflicts=conf,forbidden=forbidden,runtime=time.time()-start)
if status==z3.sat:
 model=s.model();selected=[[a for a,x in enumerate(v) if z3.is_true(model.eval(x))] for v in vs]
 H=[E for i,fam in enumerate(families) for a,E in enumerate(fam) if a in selected[i]]

 maxscore=max(sum(good[i,c[i],j,c[j]] for i in range(t) for j in range(i)) for c in itertools.product(*selected));assert maxscore<5
 out.update(selected=[[sorted(families[i][a]) for a in A] for i,A in enumerate(selected)],maxscore=maxscore)

import itertools,z3,time,json
start=time.time();r=4;n=13;weights=[-10]*5+[1]*4+[10]*4
E=list(itertools.combinations(range(n),r));idx={e:i for i,e in enumerate(E)};vs=[z3.Bool('e%d'%i) for i in range(len(E))];bs=[z3.Bool('b%d'%i) for i in range(len(E))];s=z3.Solver();s.set(timeout=120000)
# EveryHedgeisalsoamincover(sinceintersectingrankrτr); henceHedgeweightsnonnegativeaswell.
for i,e in enumerate(E):
 complement=[v for v in range(n) if v not in e];disj=[idx[F] for F in itertools.combinations(complement,r)]
 s.add(bs[i]==z3.And([z3.Not(vs[j]) for j in disj]))
 if sum(weights[v] for v in e)<0:s.add(z3.Not(bs[i]),z3.Not(vs[i]))
 for j in disj:
  if j<i:s.add(z3.Or(z3.Not(vs[i]),z3.Not(vs[j])))
for C in itertools.combinations(range(n),r-1):
 cc=set(C);s.add(z3.Or([vs[idx[F]] for F in itertools.combinations([v for v in range(n) if v not in cc],r)]))
for a,b in itertools.combinations(range(n),2):s.add(z3.Or([bs[i] for i,e in enumerate(E) if a in e and b in e]))
print('built',len(E),'time',time.time()-start,flush=True)
status=s.check();out=dict(r=r,n=n,weights=weights,status=str(status),runtime=time.time()-start)
if status==z3.sat:
 model=s.model();H=[e for i,e in enumerate(E) if z3.is_true(model.eval(vs[i]))];B=[e for i,e in enumerate(E) if z3.is_true(model.eval(bs[i]))]
 assert all(set(e)&set(f) for e in H for f in H)
 assert all(any(not set(c)&set(e) for e in H) for c in itertools.combinations(range(n),r-1))
 assert all(any(set(p)<=set(c) for c in B) for p in itertools.combinations(range(n),2))
 assert all(all(set(c)&set(e) for e in H) for c in B)
 assert all(sum(weights[v] for v in c)>=0 for c in B) and sum(weights)<0
 out.update(H=H,B=B)
print({k:v for k,v in out.items() if k not in ('H','B')},flush=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_polar_fixed_farkas.json','w') as f:json.dump(out,f,indent=2)
